claims.explanation: Isoxsuprine is a beta-adrenergic agonist that also inhibits CDK1 (IC50 ~2.9 uM), and its selective killing pattern tracks with squamous/TP53-mutant epithelial lineages and against kidney/thyroid/PTEN-intact lines, suggesting sensitivity is driven by CDK1 dependence and adrenergic/GPCR-cAMP signaling rather than a single driver mutation. The virtual-cell signature (up EGF, CHEK2; down STUB1, PARP2) is consistent with cell-cycle and DNA-damage/checkpoint perturbation. Features most likely to predict sensitivity are high CDK1/CCNB1 expression, ADRB2 expression, and TP53 pathway loss, while intact PTEN/PIK3CA and low proliferative/checkpoint tone are protective.

features.basis: Isoxsuprine directly inhibits CDK1 (IC50 2.9 uM); high CDK1/CCNB1 expression predicts mitotic dependence
CDK1-cyclin B complex is the drug target; high cyclin B marks CDK1-addicted lines
Annotated primary target of isoxsuprine; beta-agonist signaling via ADRB2/cAMP
Damaging TP53 mutations dominate the selectively killed lines, consistent with loss of checkpoint/DNA-damage response
PTEN-mutant lines (KALS1, UACC62, 786O, HEC265) are among least affected, suggesting intact PTEN/PI3K-AKT signaling supports survival
PIK3CA-mutant gastric/breast/esophageal lines (HGC27, T47D, KYSE510, MKN1) are enriched among sensitive lines
KRAS-mutant lines (NCIH1792, LS1034, GSU) appear in the sensitive set, though also in resistant lines
STK11-mutant lung/esophageal lines (NCIH1623, TE4) are selectively killed
KEAP1-mutant lines (NCIH1623, HEC265) show sensitivity, consistent with oxidative-stress vulnerability
NF1-mutant lines (S117, BICR6, KALS1) are among least affected, suggesting RAS-MAPK activation alone is not sufficient
BRAF-mutant melanoma/thyroid/colorectal lines (K029AX, UACC62, 8305C) are largely resistant
ARID1A-mutant lines (MHHNB11, T47D) appear in sensitive set, though also in resistant KU1919
